newsitem.title: USA: Digital TV Services to sell $155 mln in junk bonds.
newsitem.headline: Digital TV Services to sell $155 mln in junk bonds.

text.p: Digital Television Services, a distributor of digital broadcast satellite service DIRECTV, plans to sell $155 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette in a 144A private placement, according to a confidential prospectus obtained by Reuters.
The issuer will guarantee interest payments for the first two years via a prefunded interest reserve.
Digital TV, a privately-held company based in Roswell, Ga., is an exclusive distributor of DIRECTV with around 88,000 subscribers.
The bonds will be issued by Digital Television Services LLC/DTS Capital Inc, a subsidiary of the company.
Sources close to the deal said it is likely to be priced by the end of July.
Pegusus Communications Corp based in Radnor, Pa., is the only other DIRECTV distributor to have tapped the high-yield bond market.
In January, Pegasus issued $100 million in 12.75 percent cumulative exchangeable pay-in-kind preferred stock due '07 via CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Corp.
